title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 38 (Punishment for personation for acquisition, etc., of securities)

content.overview: Section 38(1) makes any person liable under section 447 who (a) makes or abets an application in a fictitious name for acquiring or subscribing for securities, or (b) makes or abets multiple applications in different names or in different combinations of his name or surname for acquiring or subscribing for securities, or (c) otherwise induces directly or indirectly a company to allot, or register any transfer of, securities to him or any other person in a fictitious name. Sub-section (2) requires the provisions of sub-section (1) to be prominently reproduced in every prospectus and every form of application for securities. Where a person is convicted, the Court may order disgorgement of any gain and seizure and disposal of securities in that person’s possession; amounts received are credited to the Investor Education and Protection Fund.
content.glance: Fictitious-name applications; multiple applications in different names/combinations; inducement of allotment/transfer in a fictitious name → s. 447; must be printed in prospectus and application forms; court may order disgorgement and seizure; proceeds to IEPF.
content.study: Any person who (a) makes or abets making of an application in a fictitious name to a company for acquiring or subscribing for its securities, or (b) makes or abets making of multiple applications to a company in different names or in different combinations of his name or surname for acquiring or subscribing for its securities, or (c) otherwise induces directly or indirectly a company to allot, or register any transfer of, securities to him or to any other person in a fictitious name, shall be liable for action under section 447. The provisions of sub-section (1) shall be prominently reproduced in every prospectus issued by a company and in every form of application for securities. Where a person has been convicted under this section, the Court may also order disgorgement of gain, if any, made by, and seizure and disposal of the securities in possession of, such person. The amount received through disgorgement or disposal of securities shall be credited to the Investor Education and Protection Fund. Current-law framing: identify the form of personation; apply s. 447; note the prospectus/application-form reproduction duty; note possible court orders and IEPF credit.

sections.heading: Three forms of personation
sections.body: (a) Application (or abetment) in a fictitious name for acquiring or subscribing for securities; (b) multiple applications (or abetment) in different names or different combinations of name/surname; (c) otherwise inducing allotment or registration of transfer to a fictitious name.

sections.heading: Liability under section 447
sections.body: Conduct under sub-section (1) attracts action under section 447 (punishment for fraud).

sections.heading: Reproduction in prospectus and application forms
sections.body: The provisions of sub-section (1) shall be prominently reproduced in every prospectus issued by a company and in every form of application for securities.

sections.heading: Disgorgement, seizure and IEPF
sections.body: On conviction the Court may order disgorgement of gain and seizure and disposal of securities in the person’s possession; amounts received are credited to the Investor Education and Protection Fund.

provisions.title: Punishment for personation for acquisition, etc., of securities

examples.title: Fictitious-name application
examples.body: A person applies for IPO shares in a false name. Section 38(1)(a) engages liability under section 447.

examples.title: Multiple applications
examples.body: The same person submits several applications under different names or name combinations to obtain a larger allotment. Section 38(1)(b) is engaged.

examples.title: Prospectus reproduction duty
examples.body: A company issues a prospectus that omits the prominent reproduction of section 38(1). The company has failed to comply with section 38(2).

hypotheticals.question: Is using a relative’s genuine name with consent still personation under s. 38?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 38 targets fictitious names and multiple applications by the same person in different names or combinations. Genuine applications by different real persons are outside the personation rule; multiple applications by the same person in different names fall within it.

distinctions.title: Personation (s. 38) vs fraudulent inducement (s. 36)
distinctions.left: Fictitious identity or multiple applications to obtain securities
distinctions.right: False statements or concealment to induce investment agreements

misconceptions.trap: Only the company can complain of personation.
misconceptions.correction: Section 38 creates liability under s. 447 for the specified personation conduct; the statutory text does not limit prosecution to a company complaint.

misconceptions.trap: Section 38 only penalises the applicant and has no disclosure duty.
misconceptions.correction: Sub-section (2) requires prominent reproduction of sub-section (1) in every prospectus and every form of application for securities.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 38 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the form of personation under (a)/(b)/(c). II. Apply liability under s. 447. III. Note the prospectus/application-form reproduction duty. IV. Note possible disgorgement, seizure and IEPF credit. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Conduct type; evidence of fictitious name / multiple applications / inducement; s. 447; prospectus reproduction if relevant; disgorgement/IEPF if relevant.

examTips: List the three prohibited forms of conduct under s. 38(1).
Mention court power of disgorgement/seizure and IEPF credit.
